key_insight: The thermodynamics-based Gamma metric correlates better with tensile ductility in refractory compositionally complex alloys than the DFT-based D-parameter, while performing equally well in compression.
engineering_relevance: Gamma could help screen refractory alloys for room-temperature ductility alongside their high-temperature structural performance.
method: Combine the BCC–HCP free-energy difference, BCC (110) surface interfacial free energy, and electronegativity-corrected lattice distortion.
Compare ductility correlations with existing semi-empirical metrics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a modest improvement in tensile-ductility correlation over the D-parameter and comparable performance in compression, but provides no numerical evaluation results.
watch_item: Gamma addresses intrinsic ductility; incorporating oxygen-related embrittlement through CALPHAD-calculated oxygen solubility remains a proposed first-order extension.
paper_title: Thermodynamic Underpinnings Affecting Compressive and Tensile Plasticity in Refractory Compositionally Complex Alloys
